quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams is coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the other vehicle's headlights and lets you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you know the emergency vehicle is not heading toward you.

questions.question: The Child Restraint Law requires children under eight years old and shorter than ____ to use an approved safety seat.

options.text: 5 feet, 5 inches
5 feet
4 feet, 11 inches
4 feet, 9 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 4 feet, 9 inches
questions.explanation: Children under eight years old and shorter than 4 feet, 9 inches must be secured in a child safety seat. They should not use a regular seat belt until they are old enough.

questions.question: When you must stop at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
Slow down to check that traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet in each direction, even if you enter the intersection.
Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: If you refuse a blood alcohol test, how long will you lose your driver license?

options.text: 90 days
Six months
At least one year
At least two years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one year
questions.explanation: Washington State has an implied consent law. By driving, you agree to take a breath test. If you refuse, you lose your license for at least one year.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow tells you to turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before turning left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder
At your side mirror
Over your left shoulder
At your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder
questions.explanation: Glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to drivers.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to specific places. They are helpful when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If hit from behind, this prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At an intersection, a green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You may safely turn in the direction of the arrow.
Stop, then drive straight through.
Stop, even if turning in the direction of the green arrow.
All traffic must turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may safely turn in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. If other vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection, yield to them before turning.

questions.question: Your body processes approximately:

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks per hour.
One alcoholic drink per hour.
Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink per hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. However, many factors affect how impaired a person becomes when drinking alcohol. These include the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, body weight, food intake, and general health.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so you will never see this situation.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Before crossing, check both directions for trains on any track. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the nearest track and wait until the train passes before continuing.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space, checking traffic, and signaling, stop next to the car directly in front of your desired space. Then turn your wheel to park.

questions.question: What should you be most concerned about when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights may be out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
A tire may be damaged if you drift onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning may occur if the shoulder has water on it.
You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road ahead. If one wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not slam on the brakes or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic light is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians crossing an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers may pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed lines mean drivers next to the line may pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: When using a freeway exit ramp, do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward means they intend to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this hand signal.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming up. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side as the traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: When must you dim your high beam lights?

options.text: Within 100 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Within 250 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Within 300 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.explanation: Dim your high beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: How should you drive in a roundabout (traffic circle)?

options.text: Enter whenever you want, ignoring other vehicles and pedestrians.
Stop in the circle to yield to traffic entering from the right.
Always drive around the circle to the right.
Drive to the left around the circle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always drive around the circle to the right.
questions.explanation: Always drive clockwise (to the right) around the circle. Yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid a collision?

options.text: Stop, turn, or speed up.
Move into the other vehicle's lane.
Stay in your lane and prepare for the crash.
Drive across the left lane to the left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, turn, or speed up.
questions.explanation: You have three ways to avoid a collision: stop, turn, or speed up.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Do not cross double solid lines to pass or change lanes. You may only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.
